title: The cost record has no owned operation, no closed list and no column of its own, and the only write the legacy endpoint table gives is the valuation order of another service
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-025, its Acceptance criteria, Data, Endpoints and Permission checks tables); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.7.2, A2.7.3.1, A2.7.3.2); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1, T3.2, appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-DIS-10, R-DIS-11, R-DIS-12); _work/msr/context/S5.md (two tables, six REST operations, one event, one job)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 to 4; s8 BR1, BR7, BR8; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.2; s12.8; s13; s19. CON s2; s3; s7 AC1, AC2 and AC4; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.2; s12.8; s13
description: Neither story has a sourced surface for the cost the feature records. The Ownership Map gives S5 two tables, asset_sale and listing, and six REST operations, of which the only asset writes are the listing and the auction round; TSD S5 T3.1 gives asset no cost column except holding_cost_to_date (DF-COL-042) and T3.2 gives no list of cost kinds. The legacy endpoint table gives the feature one read and one write, and that write is POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations, which the Ownership Map ruling keeps with rwb-valuation (S1) under ASM-A6-api-6, so the write of a maintenance, insurance or custody cost is described by no source. The two stories therefore declare one additive cost write on the asset base with a HoldingCost element and a closed list of three kinds, record the cost on holding_cost_to_date, and leave the naming of the operation, the element and the list to the baseline review of the CON with the placeholder until then.
evidence: _work/msr/context/S5.md lists the tables asset_sale and listing, the operations GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetId}, GET /assets/{assetKey}, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings, POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds, one event and one job; TSD S5 T-A.1 gives API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 and no cost operation, and T-A.2 describes API-S5-003 as the valuation order with the Asset and disposal right C; FSD S5 A2.7.3.2 lists only v_ace_* asset fields and no cost field; the legacy Endpoints table gives GET /assets/{assetId} with right R and POST valuations with right C; the legacy Data table names no cost entity and the legacy message set carries no cost message.
area: Data model and contract, S5 rwb-asset with S1 rwb-valuation and P1 rwb-source-data
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the solution architect, the S1 rwb-valuation owner and the data steward
proposed: Keep the metadata rows as the plan gives them; declare one additive cost write on /api/recovery/asset/v1 with the HoldingCost element and the closed list LOV-HOLDING-COST, record the cost on holding_cost_to_date, and let step D1 decide whether the DB story of this service adds a cost table and whether API-S5-003 is re-pointed to rwb-valuation.

title: The work order to the property services vendor has no owned operation, no vendor vocabulary and no instruction element, and the plan records no contract dependency although three owners are needed
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-DIS-10, R-DIS-11, R-DIS-12: ASSET_HELD to WORK_ORDER_OPEN to ASSET_HELD, vendor on the Partner Portal, 3 working days); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.7.2 integration point AMIS, A2.7.4.4 no background event); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T5.1 INT-11 to INT-13 and INT-27, T5.2, T5.3); _work/msr/context/S5.md (connection matrix row S5, T and E cells to P7, P8, S9 and S4); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 12 (partner gateway FAPI 2.0 in front of S9, partner instruction kit used by S4, S5 and S9); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the C, I and X lists of both slices are empty)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 7; s8 BR5, BR11; s12.2; s12.5; s12.8; s13; s19. CON s2; s3; s7 AC3 and AC6; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.5; s12.8; s13
description: The held property cannot be maintained without a work order to the vendor, and no source names that surface for this service. The routing logic gives R-DIS-10 the action Raise the work order to the property services vendor on the portal and R-DIS-11 the release of the invoice within 3 working days, but the Ownership Map gives S5 no instruction operation and no partner table, the partner_instruction table is S9 rwb-partner's, and the FSD A2.7.2 names only AMIS as an integration point. The step therefore declares the work order as a partner instruction consumed from S9 through the L3 partner instruction kit of the workflow platform and behind the partner gateway, declares no vendor row, no fee and no portal address in this service, and holds the 3 working days of R-DIS-11 as a durable workflow timer. Both metadata rows carry None for the contract, integration and external classes while the rwb-partner, rwb-case and rwb-decision rows are class C in fact, so the stories build against published documents and fakes and the absence is recorded rather than repaired quietly.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-10, R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-12 give the vendor, the Partner Portal channel, the sale officer acceptance and the 3 working days; TSD S5 T5.1 gives four external interfaces, none of them a vendor portal, and T5.3 gives AssetTakenOn as the only event of the module; _work/msr/context/S5.md gives S5 one event and one workflow and shows T and E cells to P8 and S9 but names no event or operation; the plan rows of RWB-S5-E3025-APP and RWB-S5-E3025-CON carry empty C, I and X lists; the legacy story has no partner step and no vendor message.
area: Workflow and contract, S5 rwb-asset with S9 rwb-partner, P3 rwb-case and P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the S9 rwb-partner owner, the platform workflow kit owner and the P3 rwb-case owner
proposed: Raise the work order as a partner instruction through the L3 kit and the rwb-partner contract, hold the acceptance window as one durable timer, keep the metadata rows as the plan gives them, and let step D1 decide whether the three rows become C dependencies of this key.

title: R-DIS-37, the bid-in-round rule, is attached to a cost feature by the legacy criterion and the FSD, while the held-property work orders of the routing logic are R-DIS-10 to R-DIS-12
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-025, Acceptance criteria AC2); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.7.3.1 rule row R-DIS-37, A2.7.4.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T4 DISPOSAL rows R-DIS-10 to R-DIS-12); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (row R-DIS-37: ROUND_OPEN, BID_PLACED, record the bid against the round and the asset, BID_RECEIVED, auction portal)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s5 X7; s7 note on AC2; s8 BR6; s9 State transitions; s10 Authority; s19. CON s2; s8 BR11
description: The legacy feature Maintain a held property records maintenance, insurance and custody costs against the asset, yet its second criterion is Rule R-DIS-37, which records a bid against the round and the asset and moves ROUND_OPEN to BID_RECEIVED, and the FSD A2.7.3.1 carries the same rule row. The routing logic gives that rule to the auction round step and gives the held-property events WORK_ORDER_RAISED, WORK_ACCEPTED and WORK_REFUSED to R-DIS-10, R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-12. Both stories therefore keep the criterion word for word because the legacy master owns it and this story owns it, describe the bid as recorded against the round and the asset by the round operation API-S5-005 of the pricing and auction stories, evaluate R-DIS-10 to R-DIS-12 for the cost step, and record the attachment as a source conflict for step D1 rather than silently dropping or rewriting a legacy criterion.
evidence: Legacy AC2 reads Given a case in state ROUND_OPEN, When bid placed, Then record the bid against the round and the asset, Then the case moves to BID_RECEIVED; FSD S5 A2.7.3.1 repeats it as R-DIS-37 Record the bid against the round and the asset, when the event occurs, Moves to BID_RECEIVED; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DIS-37 confirms the same transition with the auction portal as channel, and rows R-DIS-10, R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-12 give the work-order transitions from ASSET_HELD; TSD S5 T4 gives R-DIS-10 to R-DIS-12 in the same state machine and API-S5-005 records an auction round and its result.
area: Rules and state machine, S5 rwb-asset with P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the P7 rwb-decision rule owner and the business analyst of S5
proposed: Keep AC2 as the legacy master gives it, evaluate R-DIS-10 to R-DIS-12 for the cost step, leave the bid to API-S5-005 and the auction stories, and let step D1 decide whether R-DIS-37 belongs to this legacy key in the Business Rules workbook or to the round feature.

title: The legacy data table names the custody of documents, which is P5's fact, and the legacy message set carries two price messages that no path of this step raises
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-025, its Data, Validation and messages tables); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1: asset has no custody field); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.7.2, A2.7.3.1, A2.13 and A2.16 for the price messages); _work/msr/context/S5.md (two tables of S5, no document table and no custody table)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s5 X5; s8 BR9; s11 Data; s14 Validation and messages. CON s14; s19
description: The legacy Data table lists document_custody with DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024 beside the asset fact, but TSD S5 gives the service no document table and no custody field, the context pack gives S5 two tables, and the document facts and their custody are P5 rwb-document's. The legacy message set likewise carries MSG-S5-001 on the floor percentage and MSG-S5-002 on the age of an appraisal, and both surfaces belong to the pricing and re-appraisal steps of this service, not to the record of a holding cost. Both stories therefore record the custody cost against the asset as a cost, read no document row, keep the two messages because the legacy set owns them and state that no path of this step raises them, and add no message of their own.
evidence: The legacy Data table row reads document_custody, id, document_id, moved_at, from_location, to_location, held_by and 1 more, DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024; TSD S5 T3.1 defines asset, listing and asset_sale only and asset has no custody field; the context pack lists asset_sale and listing as the tables of S5; FSD S5 A2.7.3.1 gives one validation rule VR-S5-007-1 with MSG-GEN-001 and no price message; the legacy message set names MSG-S5-001 and MSG-S5-002 with no path in A2.7.
area: Data and messages, S5 rwb-asset with P5 rwb-document
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the P5 rwb-document owner and the business analyst of S5
proposed: Record the custody cost against the asset, read no document row, keep the two legacy messages in the message table with the note that no path of this step raises them, and let step D1 decide whether a custody-cost field or a document reference is added to the asset in a later change.

title: No requirement id covers FEAT-AST-07 in the technical specification and the plan carries no requirement for either slice
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E3-025, its metadata table with no Requirement row); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T8: REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-005 against FEAT-AST-01, REQ-S5-006 to REQ-S5-010 against FEAT-AST-08); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the reqs list of both slices is empty)
section: APP s18 Traceability; the reqs key of both fragments. CON s18 Traceability
description: The traceability of the two stories needs one sourced requirement. The legacy story master of RWB-E3-025 carries no requirement row, the plan reqs list of both slices is empty, and TSD S5 T8 maps the ten requirement ids of the module to FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08 only, so no requirement id covers FEAT-AST-07 Maintain a held property. Both stories therefore trace to the feature id FEAT-AST-07 with the placeholder for the requirement id, cite BR-S5-007 and the four rule ids as the other requirement anchors, and record the empty plan list rather than filling it with an invented identifier.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E3-025 gives Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision only; TSD S5 T8 gives REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-005 against FEAT-AST-01 and REQ-S5-006 to REQ-S5-010 against FEAT-AST-08 with Written one epic ahead in the story column; the plan rows of RWB-S5-E3025-APP and RWB-S5-E3025-CON carry reqs as an empty list; the Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-AST-07 carries no requirement id.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the business analyst
proposed: Trace both slices to FEAT-AST-07 and let step D1 add one requirement id for the held-property feature to TSD S5 T8 and to the plan reqs lists.

title: The contract baseline has no sourced element, closed list, answer shape or event for a holding cost, a work-order instruction or a case move, and the catalogue gives the service one event only
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (naming rules, two tables, six REST operations, one event EV-22, one job, one workflow); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T4, appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.7.2, A2.7.3.1, A2.7.3.2, A2.7.4.4); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-10 to R-DIS-12, R-DIS-37)
section: CON s2 Business rationale; s7 AC2, AC3 and AC7; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.3; s12.5; s12.8; s13
description: The CON publishes shapes and the sources give it almost none of them for this step. No element of a holding cost exists in TSD S5 T3.1 or T3.2, the only cost fact is holding_cost_to_date, the list of cost kinds is nowhere, the work-order instruction has no element in any owner document, and the case move of R-DIS-10 to R-DIS-12 is named only as a transition. The event catalogue gives the service EV-22 alone, which the take-on step publishes, so no event covers a cost or a work-order state. The CON therefore declares the HoldingCost element with six properties and a closed list of three values, the instruction and the case-move rows as consumed with the placeholder for their operation names, and no event of its own, and it hands every one of those names to the baseline review with the gap and the assumption attached.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 gives asset DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 with holding_cost_to_date as the only cost field and T3.2 gives six lists, none of them a cost kind; T-A.1 gives five operations and none of them a cost or an instruction; T5.3 gives AssetTakenOn as the only event; FSD S5 A2.7.3.2 lists v_ace_* asset fields only; the context pack gives the service one event and one workflow; the legacy Endpoints table gives the read and the valuation order only.
area: Contract, S5 rwb-asset with S9 rwb-partner, P3 rwb-case and P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the solution architect and the S9 rwb-partner and P3 rwb-case owners
proposed: Publish the element, the list, the instruction row and the case-move row in the baseline review, declare no published event, and let step D1 decide whether the platform event catalogue gains a cost or work-order event for the reporting read model.

title: The connection matrix shows subscribes cells and Temporal cells towards four services, and no source names the events, the operations or the outbox library of this step
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (slide 13 connection matrix row S5: T towards P7 and towards P8 and S9, E towards S4, P8 and S9; one event EV-22); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 12 and 13 (workflow kit usage and the matrix legend); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and R5.7; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (patterns DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 only, and empty C, I and X lists)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s8 BR10; s12.3; s12.4; s12.9; s13. CON s2; s3; s7 AC7; s12.3; s12.4; s12.9; s13
description: The S5 row of the connection matrix gives the service Temporal cells towards P7, P8 and S9 and subscribes cells towards S4, P8 and S9, while the catalogue of the service names one event and no source names an event of S4, S9 or P8 that a held-property cost would consume. The pattern set of this key carries DP-03, DP-05, DP-13 and DP-19 and not DP-09, although the step writes its asset row and its outbox row in one transaction, so the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is a build dependency in fact and not in the metadata row. Both stories declare no consumed event, no published event, no Schedule and no second topic, keep the metadata rows as the plan gives them, and record the missing event names and the absent DP-09 row for step D1 so that a later reporting need raises a catalogue change rather than an invented event.
evidence: The S5 row of the slide 13 matrix reads T towards P7, T and E towards P8, T and E towards S9 and E towards S4; _work/msr/context/S5.md gives the service the events row EV-22 and the jobs row JOB-19 only; TSD S5 T5.3 gives AssetTakenOn as the only event; the plan pattern list of RWB-E3-025 is DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 gives DP-09 the H row RWB-PLT-TE006-CON that the plan does not carry.
area: Events and workflow, S5 rwb-asset with S4 rwb-litigation, S9 rwb-partner, P8 rwb-payment and the platform event library
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the platform event library owner and the solution architect
proposed: Declare no event of this step, name the outbox library as an absent H row, and let step D1 decide whether the subscribes cells of the matrix and a cost or work-order event are needed for the reporting read model.
